model_annotation:
This plot illustrates the share of employed individuals (Anteil Erwerbstätige in %) as a function of age (Alter) for four population groups defined by migration background. The x-axis represents age on a linear scale, ranging from 20 to approximately 71, with major tick labels at intervals of 10 (20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70). The y-axis represents the employment share in percent on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 100, with major gridlines and tick labels at intervals of 20 (0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100).

The black solid line, representing individuals without a migration background ("ohne Migrationshintergrund"), starts at approximately 60% at age 20, rises smoothly to a plateau of roughly 87–88% around ages 40–50, remains relatively stable through the mid-50s at around 80–85%, and then declines steeply after age 60, reaching approximately 5% by age 71. The gray solid line, representing individuals born in Germany with a migration background ("in Deutschland geboren"), begins at approximately 55% at age 20, rises with some fluctuation to around 75–88% in the age range of 25–50, shows notable variability throughout, and declines after age 60, reaching approximately 15–17% near age 71. The light blue solid line, representing individuals who immigrated by 2009 ("zugewandert bis 2009"), starts at roughly 35% at age 20, increases with considerable fluctuation to approximately 60–70% in the 25–45 age range, remains variable around 60–75% through the 50s, and then drops after age 60, reaching roughly 8–10% near age 71. The blue solid line with more pronounced fluctuations, representing individuals who immigrated since 2010 ("zugewandert seit 2010"), begins at approximately 38% at age 20, fluctuates considerably between roughly 40–70% across the age range of 25–55, shows peaks near 60% around ages 28–30 and approximately 68–70% around ages 52–53, and declines sharply after age 63, dropping to approximately 0% by ages 69–71. All four lines exhibit a general pattern of increasing employment share in younger ages, a plateau or variable middle range, and a steep decline in the 60s, though the levels and degree of fluctuation differ across groups.
